categoryName: Fresh fruit assortment for a hill township

skuLines.examples: Loose mandi Grand Naine (Paonta/Una arrivals); fresho! Banana Robusta 1 kg; ITC Farmland Banana; Dole Banana
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 500 g / 1 kg pack; 6–12 pc hand; 13–14 kg crate for canteens
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; peaks at exam/breakfast weeks and Gurpurab langar
skuLines.notes: Highest-volume single fruit line in any Indian store. Arrives green from the plains; 2–3 day hill transit means it ripens on your shelf, so order 3x/week not weekly and keep a dark holding corner. Never chill below 13°C.

skuLines.examples: Loose Yelakki; fresho! Banana Elaichi 500 g; Ninjacart Elaichi
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes at Gurpurab and Sangrand
skuLines.notes: The weaning-food banana and the standard gurdwara prasad banana. Bruises easily, 3–4 day shelf; sell from a shallow tray, not a heap.

skuLines.examples: Loose raw banana; fresho! Banana Raw Green 300 g
skuLines.notes: Sells as a vegetable, keeps 7–10 days, near-zero shrink. Fasting-day demand is the real driver.

skuLines.line: Apple — Himachal economy loose (Shimla / Kinnaur, small–medium)
skuLines.examples: Loose Shimla apple ex-Rajgarh/Solan mandi; fresho! Apple Shimla Small 1 kg; Apple Shimla 4 pc
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 1 kg / 2 kg bag; 5 kg and 10 kg boxes
skuLines.seasonality: Aug–Feb peak; CA-stored fruit stretches to May–Jun at a higher cost
skuLines.marginBand: 20–30% on mandi buys; 35–45% on farm-gate buys
skuLines.notes: Sourced 0–80 km away in season — the single highest-margin, highest-trust line in this store, and the one where 'grown here' is literally true. Mar–Jun CA-store fruit costs more and shrinks more; cut depth then rather than raising price.

skuLines.line: Apple — premium Indian (Royal Gala / Red Delicious, coloured)
skuLines.examples: Apple Royal Gala Premium 4 pc; Apple Red Delicious 2 pc; Apple Queen/Rose Premium 4 pc; Indian Apple Royal Gala Regular
skuLines.packSizes: 2 pc and 4 pc trays; 500 g–1 kg
skuLines.notes: Tray-packed fruit is what gets carried to the hospital or given to a guest. Keep it visually separate from the loose economy pile or the loose pile cannibalises it.

skuLines.line: Apple — imported (Washington / NZ Royal Gala & Queen, Fuji, Pink Lady, Granny Smith green)
skuLines.examples: Apple Washington Regular 4 pc; Regular Fuji Apple 4 pc; Apple Pink Lady 2 pc; Apple Green (Granny Smith) 2 pc
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Aug, i.e. only in the domestic-crop gap
skuLines.notes: FreshPlaza, 27 Aug 2026: the arriving domestic crop is displacing imports in mainstream channels while premium imported apples hold in organised retail. So carry imported only Mar–Aug, in 2-pc packs, never loose — a hill store cannot win a price fight against fruit grown up the road.

skuLines.examples: Papaya Medium 1 pc; Papaya Large 1 pc; loose ripe papaya
skuLines.packSizes: 1 pc (800 g–1.5 kg medium, 1.5–2.5 kg large); half, cling-wrapped
skuLines.notes: The digestion fruit — hospital diet trays, the old-age home and weaning babies all pull it. Order semi-ripe: it goes over in 2 days in a warm room. Selling wrapped halves is how you stop losing whole fruit.

skuLines.examples: Papaya Raw 500 g; loose green papaya
skuLines.notes: Bought as a vegetable and for pickle; keeps 10–14 days, so it is a safe line to over-order when a vehicle is coming anyway.

skuLines.examples: Guava 500 g; Thai Guava Pink Centre 1 pc; Thai Guava White Centre 1 pc
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 500 g pack; 1 pc for Thai
skuLines.notes: Cheapest vitamin C per rupee and a school-tiffin staple. Lower Sirmaur grows it, so freight is short. Fruit-fly damage in the monsoon is severe — grade hard at intake or you sell complaints.

skuLines.examples: Pomegranate 2 pc / 4 pc; Pomegranate Regular 1 kg; fresho! Pomegranate 500 g
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 2 pc / 4 pc; 500 g / 1 kg
skuLines.cohort: all, especially elderly and hospital visitors
skuLines.notes: The North-Indian get-well fruit — with a 280-bed charitable hospital on campus this is a structural, not seasonal, line. Hard skin survives the hill road and holds 2–3 weeks: one of the few fruits worth deliberately over-stocking.

skuLines.examples: Mosambi 4 pc; Mosambi Small 1 kg; loose mosambi
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 4 pc; 1 kg / 2 kg
skuLines.notes: Bought for juice more than for eating — the classic patient and convalescent fruit. Without a juice counter beside it, it moves slowly and rots; with one, it is a daily line.

skuLines.examples: Loose Punjab Kinnow; Orange Nagpur 1 kg; Orange Imported 4 pc (off-season)
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 1 kg / 2 kg net bag; 9–10 kg box
skuLines.notes: The winter workhorse for a Punjab-linked township, and cold hill weather works in your favour — no chill chain needed Nov–Feb. Buy by the box off the Abohar/Hoshiarpur route.

skuLines.examples: Mini Orange 3 pc; loose small kinnow; Cuties-style mesh bag
skuLines.notes: Peels without a knife, so it is the residential-school tiffin citrus. Sell it in mesh bags at the counter — 5,000 residents include roughly a thousand school children buying for themselves.

skuLines.examples: Loose Thompson seedless; fresho! Grapes Green Seedless 500 g
skuLines.notes: Needs 0–4°C or it ferments and drops. Without chill on the hill leg, expect 20%+ shrink — so run it hard Feb–Apr only, in closed 500 g punnets, and never loose in sunlight.

skuLines.line: Grapes — black / red seedless and Red Globe
skuLines.examples: Grapes Red Globe 250 g; loose Sharad Seedless; imported Crimson Seedless (Jul–Nov)
skuLines.notes: The imported window keeps grapes on shelf in the monsoon-tail months when nothing domestic is available. Vietnam opened to Chilean grapes in 2026 — supply into Asia is widening, prices should ease.

skuLines.examples: Watermelon Small 1 pc (2.5–3 kg); Kiran/Sugar Queen; wrapped half
skuLines.packSizes: 1 pc whole (2–4 kg); half and quarter, cling-wrapped
skuLines.notes: Your lowest value per kg of freight — only buy when a vehicle is already coming up. Wrapped halves and quarters are what make it work in a township where most households are 2–4 people.

skuLines.examples: Muskmelon Netted Small 1 pc; Sun Melon 1 pc; Sarda melon
skuLines.notes: Smells when it is ready and smells when it is gone — sell within 3 days of ripeness or the whole rack starts to reek.

skuLines.line: Mango — mass table varieties (Dasheri, Langra, Chausa, Safeda, Totapuri)
skuLines.examples: Chausa Mango 1 kg; loose Dasheri ex-Paonta/Dehradun belt; Safeda 3 kg box
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 1 kg pack; 3 kg / 5 kg box
skuLines.notes: The Paonta Sahib–Dehradun belt is your near source for Dasheri and Langra — hours, not days. FreshPlaza flags El Niño 2026/27 and rising disease pressure against global mango, so expect a shorter, spikier season: push boxes early rather than holding for a peak.

skuLines.examples: Alphonso Ratnagiri 1 dozen box; Kesar Gir 3 kg box; Himsagar 2 kg
skuLines.packSizes: 1 kg / 2 kg / 3 kg gift box, 6–12 pc
skuLines.notes: Sells as a gift or a parcel home, not as fruit. Take pre-orders on a board — never stock premium mango on spec in a 5,000-person captive market.

skuLines.examples: Raw Mango 250 g; Raw Mango 500 g; loose kairi by the 5 kg lot
skuLines.packSizes: 250 g / 500 g; 5 kg and 10 kg pickle lots
skuLines.notes: The one mango line that moves in bulk — married staff households and both canteens buy 5–10 kg lots for aam ka achaar and panna in a two-week window. Announce the date; do not wait to be asked.

skuLines.examples: Muzaffarpur Shahi litchi 1 kg; Dehradun/Paonta litchi 500 g
skuLines.notes: 3–5 day shelf and it browns visibly. Paonta valley grows it, so the freight leg is short — buy small and repeat daily rather than one big consignment.

skuLines.examples: Rajgarh/Habban farm-gate peach; Shan-e-Punjab; flat UFO peach trial pack
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 6–8 pc tray; 4 kg farm crate
skuLines.notes: Rajgarh is literally known as the Peach Valley — this is grown within 0–15 km of the store. Best margin and best story you will ever have on a fruit rack. Flat 'UFO' peaches are the 2026 novelty in Indian trade press and worth a trial tray.

skuLines.line: Plum — local Santa Rosa/Black Amber + imported Chinese
skuLines.examples: Local Santa Rosa; Indian Plum 1 pack; Chinese Black President / Black Gemstone / Angelino; Plum Imported 6 pc
skuLines.packSizes: loose per kg; 500 g; 6 pc tray
skuLines.notes: FreshPlaza, Aug 2026: Chinese plums (Black President, Black Gemstone, Angelino, and Golden Autumn Red coming) now bridge Aug–Oct after Indian plums finish — so plum need not leave the shelf in autumn. 55–65 mm imported fruit is what sells.

skuLines.examples: Local Sirmaur/Kinnaur khubani; New Castle variety
skuLines.notes: 2–4 day shelf. Same-day sell or send the tail to drying — dried khubani then becomes a shelf-stable line instead of a write-off.

skuLines.examples: Pear Indian Babbu Gosha 1 kg; Indian Pear/Naspathi 500 g; Indian Nakh Pear 500 g
skuLines.notes: The monsoon fruit that actually survives a wet hill road — hard Patharnakh holds 2 weeks while everything soft is failing. Stock it deep Jul–Sep; it is the answer to 'there is no fruit in the shop' during the rains.

skuLines.examples: Pear Green Imported 2 pc / 4 pc; Pear Beauty 2 pc; Belgian Conference pear
skuLines.notes: Fills the winter gap after local pear ends. Belgian Conference and organic-pear programmes have been pushed into India by importers since 2022 — availability is now routine.

skuLines.examples: Loose chikoo; fresho! Sapota 500 g
skuLines.notes: Soft, sweet, needs no chewing — the old-age-home and weaning fruit. Arrives hard, ripens in 3–4 days, then goes in a day; hold half the consignment back.

skuLines.examples: Loose sitaphal; Balanagar variety
skuLines.notes: Ripens overnight and collapses the next day. Buy tight, sell within 24–48 hours of arrival, price to clear on day two.

skuLines.examples: Pineapple 1 pc; Queen variety; wrapped ring tray
skuLines.packSizes: 1 pc whole; 200–300 g cut ring tray
skuLines.notes: Keeps 5–7 days whole, which is rare among tropicals — a reliable monsoon line. Cutting it doubles the margin and rescues fruit that is going over.

skuLines.examples: Tamarind Sweet 225 g; Thai sweet tamarind pack
skuLines.notes: Pure child impulse. Put it at the billing counter, not on the fruit rack — a residential school of 5–18-year-olds is the entire market for it.

skuLines.examples: Amla 100 g / 250 g; loose amla for murabba lots
skuLines.packSizes: 100 g / 250 g / 500 g; 5 kg murabba lot
skuLines.notes: Two demands, both bulk: daily juice and the once-a-year murabba/pickle batch. Post a Nov–Dec 5 kg lot rate; married staff households will pre-book.

skuLines.examples: Loose ber; Umran / Gola variety
skuLines.notes: Cheap, dry-skinned, travels well and sells to children by the fistful. Zero cold-chain need.

skuLines.line: Local micro-season fruits (jamun, phalsa, karonda, shahtoot/mulberry, kafal, wild peach)
skuLines.examples: Karonda 250 g; loose jamun; phalsa; local shahtoot; hill kafal
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jul, each variety a 2–3 week window
skuLines.notes: Bought from village suppliers by the basket: no freight, no mandi commission, no competition. The highest-margin fruit in the store and the reason residents walk in to see what has arrived. 1–3 day shelf, so price to clear the same day.

skuLines.examples: HP-grown Hachiya/Fuyu persimmon; loose amlok
skuLines.notes: Grows in the same Himachal belt, so cost is low. Half your residents will not recognise it — a cut sample plate on the counter is the difference between selling out and writing it off.

skuLines.line: Kiwi — green (Zespri / Chile / Iran imported + HP-grown)
skuLines.examples: Kiwi Green Imported 3 pc; Kiwi Green Zespri 3 pc; Zespri SunGold 3 pc; local HP kiwi (Nov–Dec)
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; sharp spike Aug–Nov (dengue / low-platelet season)
skuLines.notes: In India kiwi is a medicine purchase, not a fruit purchase — dengue and low-platelet demand peaks in exactly the monsoon-tail weeks when the road is worst. Keep 2–3 trays on shelf even in dead months; a 280-bed hospital plus 5,000 residents guarantees the call comes. Sell as 3-pc packs, never loose.

skuLines.line: Dragon fruit (white and red flesh, Indian-grown)
skuLines.examples: Dragon Fruit 300–400 g; Red Flesh Dragon Fruit 1 pc; Gujarat/Maharashtra 'kamalam'
skuLines.notes: Now grown in India at scale (Gujarat, Maharashtra, the North-East), which is why it costs a third of what it did in the import era and why imports are falling. 7–10 day shelf makes it one of the few genuinely stockable exotics for a hill store.

skuLines.examples: Avocado Imported Medium 150–200 g; Hass; Coorg green avocado
skuLines.notes: FreshPlaza, Aug 2026: Kenya's export campaign is being held up by Gulf, India and China demand — India is now a mainstream avocado destination. Two real buyers here: gym/hostel students, and mashed avocado as a baby first food. Arrives rock-hard: run a 3–5 day ripening shelf or customers will call it a bad fruit.

skuLines.examples: Blueberry 125 g; Peruvian/Chilean imported punnet; Indian hill-grown trial
skuLines.notes: Peruvian exports are up 65–74% in 2026/27 and Chilean frozen blueberry up 23% — the price has finally come into range for a non-metro shelf. But it needs 2–4°C: 7–10 days chilled, dead in a day warm. Do not stock this without working refrigeration.

skuLines.examples: Local HP cherry (Jun); Cherry Imported 100 g; Reid Fruits Tasmanian (Dec–Feb); Turkish/Chilean cherry
skuLines.notes: Local Himachal cherry in June is a short, cheap, high-margin window; imported cherry in Dec–Jan is a gifting item at 5–10x the price. Tasmanian and Chilean programmes are actively growing their India brands in 2026.

skuLines.examples: Mahabaleshwar strawberry 200 g; local HP/Solan-belt punnet; Winter Dawn
skuLines.notes: The hill climate is an asset here — Solan-belt and local polyhouse berries land in hours, not days, in Jan–Mar. Punnet only, never loose, and never restacked. Off-season, sell frozen instead of nothing.

skuLines.examples: Grape fruit Imported 1 pc; local chakotra
skuLines.notes: A diet/diabetic-shelf item with a 2–3 week shelf life — almost no shrink risk, so a safe two-piece facing.

skuLines.line: Jackfruit — raw kathal pieces + ripe segments
skuLines.examples: Loose raw kathal 500 g; ripe jackfruit segment tray
skuLines.packSizes: 500 g raw pieces; 200–300 g ripe segment tray
skuLines.notes: Raw kathal moves to the canteens as a vegetable in bulk; ripe segments in a wrapped tray are the value-add. Whole fruit is unsellable to a 3-person household — always cut.

skuLines.line: Coconut — dry whole with husk (ritual / prasad)
skuLines.examples: Coconut Small 1 pc; Coconut Small With Husk 1 pc; loose gola
skuLines.packSizes: 1 pc; 5 / 10 pc bundles for the gurdwara
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes on Gurpurab, Sangrand, exam days, weddings and any Akhand Path
skuLines.notes: This is a religious-articles line that happens to live in the fruit rack. Keeps for months, near-zero shrink, and being out of stock on a Gurpurab in a Kalgidhar Trust township is the one fruit stockout residents will actually remember. Keep a floor quantity and never let it break.

skuLines.examples: Tender Coconut 1 pc; trimmed/shaved tender coconut
skuLines.notes: Effectively prescribed for patients and for summer dehydration — the hospital and the old-age home are the steady demand. Very heavy and low-value per kg, so only bring it up on a vehicle that is already running.

skuLines.examples: Dates Kimia with Seed 1 pack; Mazafati fresh dates; organic Medjoul
skuLines.seasonality: Aug–Nov fresh crop; chilled year-round; spikes at fasting and langar dates
skuLines.notes: Modern trade shelves this in Fresh Fruits, not dry fruit (BigBasket lists Kimia under Fresh Fruits). A Sikh-household staple for prasad, fasting and langar. Trade press flags organic dates as the steadiest-growing dried-fruit line of 2026. Keep chilled or it weeps.

skuLines.examples: Lemon 150 g / 250 g; local galgal by the kg; kagzi nimbu
skuLines.packSizes: 150 g / 250 g / 500 g; 5–10 kg pickle lots
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; galgal Nov–Feb; lemon price spikes Apr–Jun
skuLines.notes: Galgal is a Himachal specialty grown locally — Nov–Jan pickle and squash demand runs to 5–10 kg per household, which is a bulk selling window most stores miss. Ordinary lemon is a daily must and shrinks fast in a warm room; buy small and often.

skuLines.line: Cut fruit bowl / fruit chaat pack (mixed, wrapped, dated)
skuLines.examples: Mixed fruit bowl 200 g; fruit chaat pack; fresho! cut fruit tray
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; peaks in summer and exam weeks
skuLines.notes: Both the margin engine and the shrink sink: yesterday's grade-B apple, papaya and pineapple become today's ₹60 bowl. BigBasket now runs Cut Fruit as its own sub-category. Requires a chilled display, a same-day sell-by rule and a written hygiene SOP — and it maps directly onto the two canteens, the hostel mess and the hospital's diet trays.

skuLines.examples: Pomegranate Peeled 200 g; peeled sweet-lime segments; ready jackfruit segments
skuLines.notes: BigBasket carries this as a distinct line. 24-hour shelf, chilled only. The real customers are the old-age home, patients and anyone with arthritic hands — deshelling a pomegranate is exactly the work this pack removes.

skuLines.line: Fruit gift basket / hamper (assembled to order)
skuLines.examples: ₹300 get-well basket; ₹800 guest basket; ₹1,500 fruit-and-dry-fruit hamper
skuLines.packSizes: small / medium / large basket, 2–6 kg mixed
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab, Parents' Day, convocation, VIP visits, and continuously for hospital visits
skuLines.notes: Being the only outlet for 5,000 people also means being the only place to buy a get-well or a guest gift. A ribbon, a basket and a card turn ₹350 of ordinary fruit into ₹700 with no extra shrink — and it consumes the premium tray-pack apples and imported pears that otherwise sit.

skuLines.line: Institutional bulk pack (crate / box for canteens, mess, langar, hospital)
skuLines.examples: Banana 13–14 kg crate; apple 10 kg box; kinnow 9–10 kg box; watermelon by the piece-lot
skuLines.packSizes: full crate / full box / 5 kg lot
skuLines.cohort: students, university, staff (via canteens, mess, langar and hospital)
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; heavy at Gurpurab langar and school reopening
skuLines.notes: The canteens, hostel mess, langar and hospital are where the tonnage is, and they buy by the box at thin margin. Quote them on a separate institutional rate card — if the box rate and the retail rate sit on the same board, your retail price gets benchmarked to wholesale and the whole category's margin goes.

skuLines.line: Frozen fruit and fruit pulp (road-closure cover)
skuLines.examples: Frozen Mixed Berries 200 g; Frozen Blueberry 200 g; Frozen Strawberry 200 g; mango pulp 850 g tin
skuLines.packSizes: 200 g / 500 g / 1 kg frozen; 850 g pulp tin
skuLines.seasonality: monsoon and any week the hill road is cut
skuLines.notes: This is insurance, not assortment: in a Jul–Sep road closure, frozen fruit and pulp are the only fruit in the building. Needs reliable freezer space and a generator-backed plug — a thaw-refreeze cycle turns the whole stock into a write-off.

skuLines.examples: Apple Organically Grown Small 1 kg; Banana Robusta Organically Grown 500 g; Pomegranate Organically Grown 500 g
skuLines.notes: BigBasket now carries organic apple, banana and pomegranate as standard lines, so the format is proven. On a campus with its own land and a trust that runs organic-farming programmes, the honest and stronger claim is 'grown here, this is who grew it' — do not print a certification word you cannot produce a certificate for.

trends2026: Apple has split into two shelves: FreshPlaza (27 Aug 2026) reports the arriving domestic crop pushing imported apples out of mainstream channels on price, while premium imported varieties (NZ Royal Gala and Queen, Fuji, Pink Lady) hold in organised retail on sweetness, crunch, appearance and branded assurance. The buying implication is depth in local fruit Aug–Feb, and imported only in 2-pc packs in the Mar–Aug domestic gap.

Chinese plums now bridge the autumn plum gap. Only 4–5 of ~30 Chinese varieties travel to India — Black President (late May–Jul), Black Gemstone (late Jul–early Aug), Angelino and red types — arriving 55–65 mm, with European prunes, Golden Autumn Red and Ruby Plum expected next. An extended Indian domestic plum season in 2026 delayed and squeezed them, but plum no longer has to leave the shelf in Aug–Oct.

Berries are de-luxing. Peruvian blueberry exports rose 65–74% in 2026/27 and Chilean frozen blueberry exports 23%, dropping fresh 125 g punnets and frozen 200 g packs into a price band a non-metro store can actually stock — the constraint is now refrigeration, not landed cost.

Avocado has gone mainstream-adjacent in India. Kenya's 2026 export campaign is being sustained by Gulf, India and China demand while Europe falters on 34-day transits, and Indian Coorg supply is rising. Retail use has broadened from HORECA to gym/student buyers and to mashed avocado as a baby first food.

India is growing its own 'exotics' and imports of them are falling — dragon fruit ('kamalam') in Gujarat/Maharashtra/the North-East, rambutan and mangosteen on the west coast, kiwi in Himachal, and a government push on 20 indigenous and globally popular exotic crops. Mid-price exotics are now stockable inland, not just in metros.

Cut fruit is a category, not a tactic. BigBasket runs 'Cut Fruit & Tender Coconut' as its own sub-category with peeled pomegranate arils and tender coconut as fixed lines; q-commerce has normalised wrapped, dated, single-serve fruit at 40–55% gross versus 20–30% on whole fruit.

Climate volatility is shortening and shifting the windows. FreshPlaza flags El Niño 2026/27 plus rising disease pressure against global mango, historic Mexican mango losses, and growers investing in orchard infrastructure against extreme weather; buyers are being told outright that predicting each region's high and low seasons is getting harder. Plan by arrivals, not by the calendar.

Organised retail is arriving in tier-2/3 India — Carrefour opened its first Indian store (Greater Noida West, 15,000+ SKUs) in 2026, Kashmir added CA-storage capacity and a new fruit-and-vegetable mandi, and no-added-sugar dried fruit and organic dates are the fastest-growing adjacent lines. Rural captive markets will be price-compared against a modern-trade shelf within a couple of years.
adjacentServices: Fresh juice counter beside the citrus rack (mosambi, orange, galgal, watermelon) — the thing that makes sweet lime a daily line instead of a rotting one
Cut-fruit bowls and fruit chaat packs supplied daily to both canteens, the hostel mess and the hospital's diet trays — converts grade-B fruit into 40–55% margin
Fruit gift baskets and hampers for hospital visits, guest and VIP gifting, Gurpurab, Parents' Day and convocation — the only such outlet within 30–50 km
Standing orders / subscriptions: a fruit-a-day tray for staff families, the old-age home, the widows' home and hospital diet trays
Institutional supply contracts with a separate rate card: banana and apple by the crate for school breakfast, seasonal fruit by the box for langar and prasad
Local farm procurement desk buying Rajgarh peach, plum, apricot, persimmon, galgal, guava and micro-season fruit at farm gate within 0–30 km — the store's structural margin advantage
Ripening and holding room for banana, mango and avocado, so the shelf is not hostage to arrival condition after a 2–3 day hill leg
Surplus-to-preserve conversion: amla murabba, galgal and raw-mango pickle, plum and strawberry jam, dried apricot and apple rings — turns shrink into shelf-stable stock
Pre-order / weekly indent board for exotics and premium boxes (Alphonso, blueberry, imported cherry) so ₹300–1,200 SKUs are never bought on spec
Frozen fruit and pulp reserve as declared monsoon road-closure cover, held on a generator-backed freezer
Nutrition tie-in with the 280-bed charitable hospital and the academy mess — a kiwi/pomegranate/papaya 'patient pack' and a school fruit-day slot
Fruit-and-dry-fruit gifting hampers timed to academic events, plus a wholesale door for the two canteens' own retail counters
